note: The signal is SEVERAL writers on one repo at once. Negatives are ordinary git questions with a single author, which is most git questions.

queries.query: i've got three agent sessions going in the same repo and one of them just committed a file another one had staged. what's the safe way to commit when i can't be sure the index is mine
someone rebased our shared branch and now a commit i made this morning has just vanished. it's not in the log at all and the sha i wrote down doesn't resolve
about to clean up a bunch of stray assets in the project folder but half of them might belong to whoever is working on the vegetation pass. how do i not delete their stuff
two of us have the unreal editor open on the same .umap and it's an LFS binary so it can't merge. what's the protocol here
i need to undo my last two commits but keep the changes in my working tree. i'm the only one on this repo
queries.why: Ordinary single-author git. The whole premise of this skill is other writers.

queries.query: what's the difference between git reset --soft and --mixed, i can never remember which one keeps things staged
queries.why: A definitional question with a short answer; no coordination problem.

queries.query: our team keeps getting merge conflicts in package-lock.json every time two people add a dependency. is there a way to stop that
queries.why: Genuinely close - several writers - but it is a mergeable text file with a known lockfile answer, not the unmergeable-binary coordination problem.

queries.query: i want to commit only the three files i changed for this feature, not the other stuff sitting dirty in my tree
queries.why: Near-miss on scoped-commit, which owns staging discipline for a single author.
